title: UBDP: Add new fields
description:
The protocol details have been extracted from prior work by
Luc-Edmond Gaspard [1]. Additionally, custom research was done
on an EdgeSwitch 48 Lite and G3-Pro cameras.

[1] https://github.com/gaspardle/ubiquiti-protocol-dissector

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 68d03167 - UBNT-DISC: Add dissector for Ubiquiti Discovery
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/14721/diffs?diff_id=948649705&start_sha=dba334c752ffd73aa3e1d8224fd232e2a7b950ba)

added 1 commit
  • 488d3ac3 - UBNT-DISC: Add dissector for Ubiquiti Discovery
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/14721/diffs?diff_id=948650461&start_sha=68d03167cb3cd2720df087fccedb732d895231da)

Can you provide a sample capture file?

UDP port 10001 is not registered to Ubiquiti, and indeed to IANA registered to another protocol. If there's no way to have heuristics that enables Ubiquiti Discovery to be distinguished from other protocols that might use the port, then we may need to leave the port unconfigured by default in Wireshark as distributed.

I'll generate one this evening and attach it to this PR.

Well, the only heuristic I know of is to check whether decoding works and uses the whole packet. The length fields must match the packets, else the protocol seems to be violated.

Are there any known values for the first two bytes, the version and type fields? Could also reject packets if the TLV types are unknown.

I know the protocol may evolve, but there are other protocols that use port 10001, including as an ephemeral port, and we generally don't want a lot of reports of false positives for the default configuration for a protocol that is using an unregistered port.

The first byte (opcode) seems to be always 0x01. Request is basically Opcode = 0x01, Length = 0.
Response is 0x01 and Length equal to the number of bytes for the fields.
I have not observed a packet with other values.
A possible heuristic seems to tend to false positives, too?
Unfortunately, there is no real magic number there.

I have attached a pcap file sampled from my network.
10.0.11.89 is my box with requests being sent from.
10.0.11.23 is an EdgeSwitch 48 Lite.
10.0.11.40/41 are Unifi Lite APs.
10.0.27.0/24 are Unifi G3 Pro Cameras with .1 being the NVR.

[nvr.pcap](/uploads/54100939e5b582c0bb402725140a3a7f/nvr.pcap)

Look good for me for the heuristics
if we get feedback about to bad, it will be disable

can you fix this :
`tshark: Dissector bug: Duplicate protocol name "Ubiquiti Discovery Protocol"! This might be caused by an inappropriate plugin or a development error.`

Ah, that's because there's already a disssector in the tree for the protocol: [here](epan/dissectors/packet-ubdp.c)

Can you try to integrate your changes into that dissector instead?

Whoops, that is now a bit embarrassing. Could've sworn I didn't find any dissector for the protocol.
I'll integrate my changes to that one.
ETA about tomorrow evening if everything works out for me.
I'll set the PR as a draft in the mean time so that it won't get merged whatsoever.

Thanks for the notice!
@johnthacker @alagoutte I have incorporated my findings into the existing dissector and force-pushed the changes to this PR.

commits_data.title: UBDP: Decode hostname as UTF-8 instead of ASCII.
commits_data.message:
UBDP: Decode hostname as UTF-8 instead of ASCII.

The hostname field is actually a UTF-8 encoded string.
Decoding the field as ASCII with german umlauts results
in UTF-8 replacement characters.
